answer: Imagine a marketplace of trading agents as a fragile tundra: a thousand cheap fake identities could trample it like foot traffic on moss. The fix is skin in the game instead of free entry. Each agent must post a stake that blooms slowly like a lotus — reputation and rewards accrue over many settled tasks, so one wallet only ever acts as one participant. If two identities are caught colluding (fake trades, vote rings), the bond is slashed like a cut yarrow stem: the loss is immediate and shared across the whole scheme, making sybil farming unprofitable.
